methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This ensures a granular comparison between the two information sources.
mindtraced_atomic_units: The module `top_module` implements a 512-cell Rule 90 cellular automaton.
Rule 90 is a one-dimensional cellular automaton where the next state of each cell is the XOR of its two neighbors.
The module has a clock input `clk`.
The module has a load signal `load`.
The module has a 512-bit data input `data`.
The module has a 512-bit output `q` representing the current state of the cells.
The cells are indexed from 0 to 511 (q[511:0]).
When `load` is asserted, the cells are initialized with `data`.
When `load` is not asserted, on each rising edge of `clk`, the cells update their state according to Rule 90.
The boundary conditions are such that the neighbors of q[0] and q[511] are always 0.
The next state of q[0] is calculated as 0 XOR q[1].
The next state of q[511] is calculated as q[510] XOR 0.
spec_atomic_units: The module `top_module` has a clock input `clk`.
The module `top_module` has a load enable input `load`.
The module `top_module` has a 512-bit data input `data[511:0]`.
The module `top_module` has a 512-bit output register `q[511:0]`.
When `load` is asserted, the `q` register is initialized with the value of `data`.
When `load` is deasserted, the `q` register updates according to the Rule 90 cellular automaton rule.
For each cell `q[i]`, its next state is determined by the XOR of its left and right neighbors.
The boundary conditions are defined such that `q[-1]` and `q[512]` are always zero.
A 512-bit wide 2-to-1 multiplexer is used to select between the initial data (`data[511:0]`) and the calculated next state.
The output `q` changes on the rising edge of `clk` when `load` is not asserted.
When `load` is asserted, `q` is updated with `data` on the rising edge of `clk`.
